meta_desc: Step-by-step NCERT Exemplar Class 12 solution to evaluate cos[cos⁻¹(−√3/2)+π/6], with cos⁻¹(−√3/2)=5π/6 and answer −1, plus a free 8-question quiz.

quiz.title: Inverse Cosine Principal Values Quiz
quiz.intro: Eight questions on principal values of cos⁻¹ with negative arguments and on evaluating cos of an inverse-cos-plus-angle expression. Pick an answer for each, then press Check my score.
quiz.about: Class 12 Inverse Trigonometric Functions — cos⁻¹ principal values

questions.explanation: cos⁻¹ takes values in [0, π]. Since cos(5π/6) = −√3/2 and 5π/6 lies in that range, cos⁻¹(−√3/2) = 5π/6.

questions.q: What is the principal-value range of cos⁻¹ x?
questions.explanation: The principal value branch of cos⁻¹ is the closed interval [0, π]. That is why cos⁻¹ of a negative number lands in (π/2, π].
cos⁻¹(−√3/2) = 5π/6, so the angle is 5π/6 + π/6 = π. Then cos π = −1.
cos(2π/3) = −1/2 and 2π/3 is in [0, π], so cos⁻¹(−1/2) = 2π/3.
cos π = −1 and π is the largest value in the range [0, π], so cos⁻¹(−1) = π.

questions.q: For x in [−1, 1], cos⁻¹(−x) equals which of these?
questions.explanation: The standard identity is cos⁻¹(−x) = π − cos⁻¹ x. For example, cos⁻¹(−√3/2) = π − cos⁻¹(√3/2) = π − π/6 = 5π/6.
cos(3π/4) = −1/√2 and 3π/4 lies in [0, π], so cos⁻¹(−1/√2) = 3π/4.
cos⁻¹(−1/2) = 2π/3, so the angle is 2π/3 + π/3 = π. Then cos π = −1.

faq.q: Why is cos⁻¹(−√3/2) equal to 5π/6 and not −π/6 or 7π/6?
faq.a: Because the principal value of cos⁻¹ must lie in [0, π]. Both −π/6 and 7π/6 fall outside that interval, so the only valid answer is 5π/6, which is where the cosine equals −√3/2 within the allowed range.

faq.q: How do you evaluate cos[cos⁻¹(−√3/2) + π/6] step by step?
faq.a: First find cos⁻¹(−√3/2) = 5π/6. Add the extra angle: 5π/6 + π/6 = 6π/6 = π. Finally take the outer cosine: cos π = −1. So the whole expression equals −1.

faq.q: What is the quick rule for cos⁻¹ of a negative number?
faq.a: Use cos⁻¹(−x) = π − cos⁻¹ x. So cos⁻¹(−√3/2) = π − cos⁻¹(√3/2) = π − π/6 = 5π/6. This keeps the answer inside the [0, π] range automatically.

faq.q: Why does cos⁻¹ have range [0, π] instead of the same range as sin⁻¹?
faq.a: Cosine is one-to-one and covers every value from 1 down to −1 exactly once on [0, π], so that interval is chosen as its principal branch. sin⁻¹ uses [−π/2, π/2] for the same reason applied to sine.
